newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel - bank merger good for jobs and for Munich.
newsitem.headline: Waigel - bank merger good for jobs and for Munich.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Monday the planned merger of Bayerische Vereinsbank AG with Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG would cost fewer jobs than if a larger bank had bought either of the two banks.
Waigel told a news conference that politicians would have to influence the two banks to maintain as many jobs as possible.

"It has been clear to me for years that there would be such a solution. The decision is right and positive for Munich as a financial centre. Any other decision would be problematic for us and for Munich.

"If either bank had merely become a branch of another big bank, more jobs would have been lost," Waigel said. Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank announced on Monday they planned to merge, creating Germany's second largest commercial bank behind Deutsche Bank AG.
The move came after a year of intense speculation of bank mergers but the linkup between the two Bavarian banks had been just one of several scenarios predicted by analysts.
Some had expected Frankfurt-based Dresdner Bank AG to acquire Hypo-Bank. --David Crossland, Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
